question: A 55-year-old man with a history of repeated hospitalization for chronic pancreatitis comes to the physician because of difficulty walking and standing steadily. Neurological examination shows an unsteady, broad-based gait, distal muscle weakness, decreased deep tendon reflexes, and an abnormal Romberg test. His hemoglobin concentration is 11.9 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume is 89/μm3, and serum lactate dehydrogenase is 105 U/L. His serum haptoglobin is slightly decreased. A deficiency of which of the following substances is the most likely cause of this patient's findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Chronic pancreatitis" -> "malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins" -> "vitamin E (tocopherol) deficiency" -> "neurological symptoms (unsteady gait, abnormal Romberg)" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Chronic pancreatitis" -> "malabsorption" -> "vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "neurological symptoms" -> "not supported by lab findings" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Chronic pancreatitis" -> "malabsorption" -> "vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) deficiency" -> "neurological symptoms" -> "less likely given symptoms" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Chronic pancreatitis" -> "malabsorption" -> "vitamin K (phytomenadione) deficiency" -> "bleeding tendency" -> "not matching symptoms" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Chronic pancreatitis" -> "malabsorption" -> "folate deficiency" -> "anemia" -> "not matching neurological symptoms" -> 40%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including an unsteady, broad-based gait, distal muscle weakness, decreased deep tendon reflexes, and an abnormal Romberg test, suggest a neurological issue potentially related to a vitamin deficiency. The history of chronic pancreatitis can lead to malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Tocopherol (Vitamin E) deficiency is known to cause neurological symptoms such as ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, and muscle weakness, which align with the patient's presentation. The other options are less likely to cause this specific combination of neurological symptoms.
